lessons.title: Queues wait. Profiles decide who is eligible.
lessons.why: A queue with nobody whose profile includes it is a silent parking lot.
paras: You create a queue, attach hours, an outbound caller ID, and optional quick connects. Set working queue selects it. Transfer to queue places the contact. The default is 100 queues and 50 queue-channel combinations per routing profile.
Agent queues are for transfers to a person. The default cap is 10 contacts waiting on one agent queue.
points: Priority is per profile, not a property of the queue alone.
A contact can sit in a queue that is outside the hours if you never checked hours.
Callbacks still occupy the queue's logic. They need a staffed profile.
Name queues for the work, not for a person.

lessons.title: Priority, delay, and concurrency
lessons.why: Lower priority number wins. Delay keeps a second team in reserve. Concurrency is how many of each channel an agent holds.
paras: Voice concurrency is typically one. Chat can be higher. The profile lists queues per channel, and each queue-channel pair counts toward the quota of 50. Manual assignment queues have their own count of 50.
Routing criteria add steps that expire, which is the Connect version of a precision-queue step. Proficiencies are levels on predefined attributes, 10 per agent by default.
points: Delay is in seconds. A delay of 0 means eligible immediately.
Two profiles can point at one queue with different priority.
Cross-channel concurrency is a choice. A voice call plus three chats is a workload, not a free feature.
Change routing priority / age if a flow must jump the line. Use it rarely and log why.
lessons.mistake: Setting every queue to priority 1 and wondering why the overflow team is busy.

lessons.title: Hours and overrides
lessons.why: The check uses the queue's hours and the queue's time zone. Your laptop's clock is irrelevant.
paras: You get 100 hours-of-operation objects, 50 overrides each, and at most 3 associations to inherit recurring overrides. Overrides are how holidays work. An override that does not include the date you think it does is a normal incident.
Out-of-hours should say when you are open and offer a callback or a task if that is honest. Do not transfer to a queue you just proved is closed unless the queue flow also knows.
points: Check hours before Set working queue.
Publish the time zone in the prompt if you serve more than one.
Overnight hours that cross midnight need a careful read of the day boundary.
The override quota is not adjustable.
lessons.mistake: Testing hours from a browser in another time zone and trusting the result without reading the queue zone.

lessons.title: Quick connects and the flows behind them
lessons.why: A quick connect is a target plus a flow. The flow is where you record, whisper, and set attributes.
paras: User, queue, and phone-number quick connects are the three types. Queue and agent transfers use the transfer flows you attach. The default quota is 100 quick connects per instance.
A phone-number quick connect to a CUCM pilot is the supported side-by-side seam. Attributes do not survive that hop.
points: Put the quick connect on the queue the agent is actually using.
The transfer flow should set recording if the destination is still inside Connect.
External numbers need a spoken confirmation if the destination is a mobile.
Interrupt agent is the rare tool for forcing a specific agent. It is not the everyday quick connect.
lessons.mistake: A quick connect list of 100 people.
